description: Golden test vectors for the Ratifia facts hash (FN-259). Every client that computes factsHash must produce exactly these canonical strings and hashes. The API never hashes; it only compares the string a client sends at request time with the one sent at verify and consume. Change this file only together with the algorithm, in every client at once: that is a breaking protocol change.
algorithm: factsHash = lowercase hex of sha256(utf8(canonical(facts))). canonical(facts): JSON with no whitespace; object keys sorted at every level by UTF-16 code unit; arrays keep their order; strings and numbers written exactly as ECMAScript JSON.stringify writes them. undefined, NaN, Infinity, Dates, functions, bigints and class instances are refused, never hashed.

vectors.name: refund, amount changed
vectors.note: One digit changes the hash. This is the facts_mismatch case.

vectors.name: refund, keys in reverse order
vectors.note: Same sha256 as "refund": key order never matters.

vectors.name: nested objects are sorted at every level
array order matters, descending
vectors.note: Different sha256 from the ascending case: arrays are not sorted.

vectors.name: numbers
vectors.note: Numbers are written the way ECMAScript JSON.stringify writes them: 1e+21, 1e-7, and 100.0 becomes 100. Python json.dumps writes 1e+21 as 1e+21 but 100.0 as 100.0 and 1e-7 as 1e-07, so a Python client must format numbers itself. Pass large ids as strings.

vectors.name: string escaping
vectors.note: Control characters become \uXXXX (lowercase hex); "/" is not escaped.

vectors.name: non-ASCII strings are hashed as raw UTF-8
vectors.note: Not \u-escaped. Python json.dumps escapes by default; pass ensure_ascii=False.

vectors.name: keys sort by UTF-16 code unit
vectors.note: Plain string comparison, not numeric: "10" sorts before "9", uppercase before "_" before lowercase.

vectors.name: astral-plane keys sort by UTF-16 code unit, not code point
vectors.note: U+1F600 is the surrogate pair D83D DE00, which sorts before U+FF5A. A code-point sort (Python sorted(), Go, Rust) puts it after and gets a different hash.

facts.subject: Your refund
facts.body: We have refunded $620.00 to your card.
